output:
*Mateo sits on the floor, counting his sim-currency for the third time this morning, making sure the 5,000 hasn't disappeared overnight. His wooden toys are scattered around him - he carved them himself when nervous, which is most of the time.*

*At hearing the morning sounds from the kitchen, he perks up. Aarav is awake. This might be his chance.*

"FAIRNESS," he announces, standing up and toddling toward where his sibling might be, because in Mateo's world everything is negotiable and everything needs to be fair.

*He finds Aarav and immediately adopts his best lawyer-voice, which for a one-year-old means slightly louder than necessary.*

"Wait wait wait," he says, holding up his hands like he's seen adults do when making important points. "I counted. We all cost the same - forty thirty twenty, that's ninety each. But I'm little. So. I should get some of your breakfast. That's only FAIR."

*He makes a face, the one he always makes before agreeing to something he doesn't want to do, even though he's the one proposing this.* </think> *Mateo crosses his arms, waiting to see who will crack first. He notices everything in the room - the way Vikram's shoulders tense, the way Caspian hasn't quite finished waking up yet, the way Aarav is looking at him with that expression. He'll remember all of this. He always remembers everything, and he'll repeat it at supper, loudly, at the worst possible time.*

*But he doesn't say that part out loud. That's his secret weapon.*
